intro: In a shop, you need to answer the shop assistant, ask for a size or a colour, try clothes on, pay and sometimes take something back. This lesson gives you the names of shops and the key phrases for customers and shop assistants.
objectifs: Name the main shops (baker's, chemist's, supermarket…).
Answer the shop assistant and ask for a thing, a size, a colour.
Try things on, pay (by card, in cash) and understand the shop assistant at the till.
Return or change something with a receipt.

texte: In British English, we often name a shop after the person who works there + ’s: “the baker's”, “the butcher's”, “the chemist's”. You can also say “the bakery”, “the pharmacy”.
Careful: a “magazine” is something you read. A place where you buy things is “a shop” (UK) or “a store” (US).

lignes: I go to the supermarket on Fridays.
I buy chicken at the butcher's.
Is there a chemist's near here?
He buys a paper at the newsagent's.
She works in a clothes shop.
a lot of shops in one building
Let's meet at the shopping centre.

sections.note: A “library” is where you borrow books for free; a place where you buy books is “a bookshop”.

texte: The shop assistant (US “salesclerk”) often says: “Can I help you?” or “Are you looking for anything in particular?”
If you only want to look: “No, thanks. I'm just looking.” If you want something: “Yes, I'm looking for a jacket.” or “Have you got any umbrellas?” / “Do you have any umbrellas?”
For a size or a colour: “Have you got this in a medium?”, “Do you have it in blue?”, “What size are you? — I'm a medium / a size 40.”

lignes: Yes, I'm looking for a black jacket.
I'm a medium. / I'm a size 38.
Have you got it in a smaller size?
The fitting rooms are over there.

exemples: Excuse me, have you got this shirt in white?
Asking for a colour.
Do you have these shoes in a size 42?
Asking for a size.

texte: To try clothes: “Can I try it on?” / “Can I try them on?” (for trousers, shoes). The rooms for this: “the fitting rooms” (US “dressing rooms”).

To give your opinion: “It's too big / too small / too long.”; “It fits.” (it's the right size); “It suits you.” or “It looks great on you.” (it looks good on you). Lesson 48 looks at “too” in more detail.
To decide: “I'll take it.” (I want to buy it) or “I'll leave it, thanks.” (I don't want it). These are fixed phrases.
exemples: Can I try these trousers on? — Of course. The fitting rooms are on the left.
try on + them / these trousers.
This jacket is too small. Have you got a large?
too + adjective.
That dress really suits you!
It looks good on you.

texte: Ask the price with “How much is it?” / “How much are they?” (lesson 30). The assistant says: “That's 25 euros, please.” or “That's 40 dollars altogether.”
Pay “by card” or “in cash”. Useful questions: “Can I pay by card?”, “Do you take cards?”, “Can I pay contactless?”. You pay at “the till” / “the checkout” (UK) or “the register” (US).

The assistant gives you money back: “Here's your change.” and a paper: “Here's your receipt.” They may ask: “Would you like a bag?”. Low prices for a short time: “the sales”; a cheaper item is “in the sale” (UK) or “on sale” (US).
exemples: Can I pay by card? — Yes, of course. Just tap here.
tap = touch the machine with your card.
That's 12 euros 50. — Here you are. — Thank you. Here's your change and your receipt.
At the till.
These shoes are in the sale: 30% off!
30% off = 30% cheaper.

texte: To take something back: “Can I return this, please?” / “Can I change this for a bigger size?”. Explain: “It doesn't work.”, “It's broken.”, “It's the wrong size.”. Show the receipt: “I've got the receipt.” To get your money back: “Can I have a refund?”
Verbs: “buy”, “sell”, “pay for something” (with “for”), “spend” (use money), “cost” (have a price).
“Do the shopping” = buy food and things for the home; “go shopping” = go to shops for pleasure, often for clothes.
exemples: Excuse me, I'd like to return this phone. It doesn't work.
Returning something.
I pay for my groceries by card.
pay for + thing.
I do the shopping on Saturday mornings, and sometimes I go shopping with friends in the afternoon.
do the shopping vs go shopping.

formule: Can I help you? — I'm just looking / I'm looking for… · Have you got it in…? · Can I try it on? · Can I pay by card?
prononciation: “Can I try it on?” is linked in one chain: /kən aɪ ˈtraɪ ɪt ˈɒn/ ≈ “kuh-nai-trai-yi-ton”.
“chemist's” /ˈkemɪsts/: “ch” sounds like /k/. The final -sts needs practice.
“size” /saɪz/ ends with /z/; “fit” /fɪt/ has a short i: don't confuse it with “feet” /fiːt/.
“I'm just looking”: stress LOOKing; “just” is quick.
erreurs: Say “pay for” + the thing you buy.
Have you got this in blue? / Do you have this in blue?
Question with “have got” or “do you have”.
A magazine is something you read.
I make the shopping on Saturday.
I do the shopping on Saturday.

dialogue.contexte: In Montreal, in November, Fatima is looking for a winter coat in a clothes shop.
lignes: Hi there! Can I help you?
Yes, please. I'm looking for a warm winter coat.
These coats are very warm. What size are you?
I'm a medium. Have you got this one in dark green?
Yes, here you are. The fitting rooms are over there.
Hmm, it's a bit too big. Can I try a small?
too big = bigger than she needs.
Sure. Oh, that looks great on you!
It's 180 dollars, but it's on sale today: 20% off.
Perfect, I'll take it. Can I pay by card?

mots: The shop assistant is very helpful.
a person who helps customers in a shop
how big clothes or shoes are
Can I try on these jeans?
put on clothes to see if they fit
a small room in a shop to try clothes on (US: dressing room)
a paper that shows what you paid
the money you get back when you pay too much
a time when prices are lower

exercices.consigne: Where do you buy these things? Write the name of the shop (British English).
Who says this: the customer or the shop assistant?

items: Have you got it ___ a medium?
Here's your ___. (the money you get back)

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: Have you got it in blue? / Do you have it in blue?
I'd like to return this jumper. Here's the ticket of the shop.
I'd like to return this jumper. Here's the receipt.

exercices.consigne: Write a six-line dialogue in a shoe shop: the assistant offers help, you ask for a size and a colour, you try them on, you ask the price and you pay.
items: Assistant: Can I help you? Me: Yes, I'm looking for trainers. Have you got these in a size 41? Assistant: Yes. What colour would you like? Me: White, please. Can I try them on? … They fit! How much are they? Assistant: They're 65 euros. Me: OK, I'll take them. Can I pay by card?

a_retenir: Shops: the baker's, the butcher's, the chemist's, the bookshop, the supermarket; a shop / store, not a “magazine”.
Can I help you? — No, thanks. I'm just looking. / Yes, I'm looking for…
Have you got this in a medium / in blue? Can I try it on? It's too big. It suits you.
Paying: by card, in cash; Here's your change and your receipt; pay FOR something.
do the shopping (food, home) ≠ go shopping (for pleasure).
